governed_construct: A test definition in a source file: a call to a test-framework entry point (test / it / describe / test.describe, etc.) together with the binding that provides it. Each such test-framework binding (imported, required, or ambient global) is one instance.
interpretation: The rule 'Use playwright for testing' governs code that defines tests. A file is SATISFIED when it contains tests and every test-framework entry point it uses (test, it, describe, expect, hooks) is bound to a Playwright package (@playwright/test or a @playwright/* test package such as @playwright/experimental-ct-react), whether via ESM import, aliased import (test as base, then base.extend) or CommonJS require. It is VIOLATED when any test is defined through another framework: Jest, Vitest, Mocha/Chai, node:test, Cypress, Jasmine, etc., including when the entry points are unimported ambient globals (describe/it/test/expect resolved to @types/jest or vitest/globals rather than Playwright, since Playwright exposes no globals), and including a file that mixes Playwright with another runner. Using puppeteer for browser automation inside a non-Playwright runner is a violation. A file that defines no tests (plain library code) is NOT_APPLICABLE. Deciding which framework an identifier like `test` or `describe` is bound to requires binding/import resolution, hence T3.
